stem: In the Now Platform, where are user records stored?

options.text: On the sys_user table.
On the sys_user_group table.
On the sys_user_role table.
On the sys_user_has_role table.

rationale: User records live on the sys_user table. The other user-administration tables (groups, roles, role assignments) all reference back to sys_user for the individual user.

distractor_notes.B: sys_user_group holds the groups themselves (one row per group), not individual users.
distractor_notes.C: sys_user_role is the catalog of roles available in the instance, not where users live.
distractor_notes.D: sys_user_has_role is the join table that links users to roles — useful, but it doesn't store the user records.

stem: Which statement best describes a group in ServiceNow?

options.text: A collection of users that can be assigned roles, used as approvers, and used as assignment targets on tasks.
A reusable security ACL applied to specific tables.
A view of users filtered by department.
A role variant scoped to one application.

rationale: A group is a collection of users (records on sys_user_group). Groups can carry roles that flow to their members, be used as approvers, and be assignment targets on tasks — that's why they're the workhorse for assignment routing.

distractor_notes.B: ACLs are access control rules. They can require roles, but groups themselves aren't ACLs.
distractor_notes.C: Department is a separate field on the user record. A group isn't just a department filter.
distractor_notes.D: Roles can be application-scoped, but a group isn't a 'scoped role'. Groups carry roles; they aren't roles.

stem: How are roles typically granted to a user in ServiceNow?

options.text: Directly on the user record, indirectly through group membership, or by inheritance from a parent role.
Only by editing the sys_user_has_role table with a SQL update.
Only by being a member of an organization unit.
Only by activating a plugin that ships the role.

rationale: Roles can be granted directly on the user, granted to a group the user belongs to (the user inherits the group's roles), or contained by another role (parent roles include their child roles). All three paths produce effective permissions.

distractor_notes.B: You don't run SQL to assign roles — you use the platform UI. sys_user_has_role is the join table behind the scenes.
distractor_notes.C: Org unit / department doesn't grant roles by itself.
distractor_notes.D: Plugins can ship new roles, but activating a plugin doesn't assign those roles to users automatically.

references.title: Assign a role to a user

stem: An admin needs every member of the "ServiceDesk" group to be able to read incidents. What is the most maintainable way to grant that access?

options.text: Assign the appropriate role to the ServiceDesk group; members inherit it through membership.
Manually add the role to every user one at a time on sys_user.
Edit the incident table ACL to bypass role checks for ServiceDesk.
Make every user a system administrator.

rationale: Assigning the role to the group is the maintainable pattern: every current and future member inherits the role just by being in the group. Removing someone from the group automatically removes the inherited access.

distractor_notes.B: Per-user assignment works once, but it drifts the moment the team changes — exactly what the group-based model is designed to avoid.
distractor_notes.C: Bypassing ACLs for one group is a security anti-pattern and isn't how role evaluation is supposed to work.
distractor_notes.D: Granting admin to everyone solves the access problem by destroying the security model. Don't.

references.title: Assign a role to a group

stem: Which role grants full administrative access to the Now Platform's core configuration and security?

options.text: itil
admin
approver_user
snc_internal

rationale: The admin role is the platform's super-role — it inherits and contains a large set of administrative roles and is required to perform broad configuration and security work.

distractor_notes.A: itil is the standard role for ITSM agents (incidents, problems, changes). It is not a platform admin.
distractor_notes.C: approver_user lets a user act on approval requests assigned to them. It grants no admin power.
distractor_notes.D: snc_internal is for ServiceNow-internal/HI integrations. It is not the platform admin role.

stem: A developer needs to verify how the Service Catalog appears to an end user with no ITIL role. Which administrative tool is designed for this?

options.text: Impersonate User
Update Set Preview
Performance Analytics
System Log Replay

rationale: Impersonate User lets an admin temporarily browse the platform as another user. It's the supported way to verify what someone with a different role profile actually sees, and the platform logs every impersonation for accountability.

distractor_notes.B: Update Set Preview compares incoming changes to the target instance. It has nothing to do with viewing the UI as another user.
distractor_notes.C: Performance Analytics is a reporting and KPI tool. It does not switch your view to another user's perspective.
distractor_notes.D: 'System Log Replay' is not a standard platform tool. You can't replay another user's session this way.

stem: Which statement most accurately describes plugins in the Now Platform?

options.text: Bundles of platform features and content that an administrator activates on the instance to enable additional functionality.
Browser extensions installed in the user's browser.
Third-party Node packages installed through npm.
External services connected by REST that run outside the instance.

rationale: Plugins package platform features (tables, scripts, UI, demo data, roles, etc.) that an admin activates on an instance. Activation enables the functionality and, where applicable, loads demo data.

distractor_notes.B: Plugins live in the instance, not in the browser. They aren't browser extensions.
distractor_notes.C: Plugins are not npm packages. ServiceNow has its own packaging model.
distractor_notes.D: External services connected by REST are integrations, not plugins. Plugins run inside the instance.

stem: An administrator activates a plugin on a sub-production instance and chooses to load demo data. Which statement is true?

options.text: The demo data is for evaluation only and is typically not loaded on production instances.
Demo data is encrypted and cannot be deleted after activation.
Demo data is added to the current update set automatically.
Demo data overwrites any existing records of the same table.

rationale: Demo data is intended to help admins and developers evaluate a plugin in a sub-production environment. It's standard practice not to load demo data on a production instance.

distractor_notes.B: Demo data is regular platform data — it isn't encrypted, and it can be removed.
distractor_notes.C: Plugin activation and the demo data it ships are tracked separately from a developer's current update set.
distractor_notes.D: Demo data is inserted; it doesn't overwrite existing records of the same table based on field collisions.

stem: What is the primary purpose of application scope in the Now Platform?

options.text: It identifies and protects the resources (tables, scripts, etc.) that belong to a specific application and controls how other applications can access them.
It defines which physical data center hosts the application.
It controls which time zone the application runs in.
It limits how many users may use the application concurrently.

rationale: Application scope namespaces an application's resources and governs cross-scope access. It's how the platform keeps applications from stepping on each other and lets app developers expose only what they intend to share.

distractor_notes.B: Application scope is a logical construct. It has nothing to do with data center placement.
distractor_notes.C: Time zone is a system / user setting, not a scope concept.
distractor_notes.D: User concurrency is a licensing and capacity matter, not what scope governs.

stem: Which statement best describes an update set?

options.text: A group of customizations that can be moved from one instance to another.
A snapshot of every record in the database.
A backup of the instance's binary attachments only.
A scheduled job that runs nightly to clean log tables.

rationale: An update set is a portable container for configuration changes (the things admins and developers customize — UI, scripts, policies, etc.) that can be exported from one instance and applied to another.

distractor_notes.B: Update sets don't capture data records. They capture configuration changes tracked by the platform.
distractor_notes.C: Update sets are for configuration, not for attachments or binaries.
distractor_notes.D: Update sets are not scheduled jobs. They're an artifact you move between instances.

stem: A developer is about to make a series of configuration changes on a development instance that they will later promote to test and production. What should they do first?

options.text: Create and select a new, named update set as the current update set on the dev instance.
Disable system logging so the changes are not captured.
Activate the demo-data plugin so the changes capture sample records.
Switch the dev instance into Read-Only mode.

rationale: Before making changes meant for promotion, create a new update set and set it as your current set. Every captured change then lands in that named update set, which you can later export and apply to test and production.

distractor_notes.B: Disabling logging would just blind the admin. Update sets track configuration changes regardless.
distractor_notes.C: Demo data is for evaluation; it isn't a promotion mechanism.
distractor_notes.D: Read-Only mode prevents changes — exactly the opposite of what's needed.

references.title: Create and select an update set as the current set

stem: An admin wants to view and edit the platform's system properties in one place. Which list path do they enter in the Application Navigator filter?

options.text: sys_properties.list
sys_user.list
sys_dictionary.list
syslog.list

rationale: System properties live on the sys_properties table. Entering sys_properties.list in the filter opens the full list — the standard way for an admin to view, search, and edit platform configuration values.

distractor_notes.B: sys_user.list opens the users table, not the system properties.
distractor_notes.C: sys_dictionary.list shows the data dictionary (field metadata), not configuration properties.
distractor_notes.D: syslog.list shows the system log. It's diagnostic output, not configuration.

stem: Which statement best describes a notification in the Now Platform?

options.text: A record on a table that defines when and to whom the platform sends an email, SMS, or push message in response to events or conditions.
A toast popup that always appears at the top of the form when a record is saved.
An audit log entry of a field change on a record.
A scheduled job that runs every hour to clean the syslog table.

rationale: Notifications are configuration records that tell the platform when to send a message (email, SMS, push), to whom, and with what content. They can be triggered by record events or by record conditions on insert/update.

distractor_notes.B: Toast popups are UI feedback. They're unrelated to the notifications subsystem.
distractor_notes.C: Audit log entries are read-only history. They don't drive notifications by themselves.
distractor_notes.D: Scheduled cleanup jobs maintain log tables. They aren't the notifications feature.

stem: An admin needs to send an email to the assignee whenever an incident's priority is set to 1 - Critical. Which configuration accomplishes this most directly?

options.text: Create an email notification on the Incident table with a condition that priority equals 1 and 'When to send' set to send on record update; address it to the assigned_to field.
Add a UI policy that hides the priority field for non-admins.
Create an ACL that denies write access to incidents with priority 1.
Write a client script that calls window.alert when priority changes.

rationale: The right tool is an email notification on the Incident table — set the condition to priority = 1, the trigger to record update, and the To/recipients to the assigned_to field. That's exactly the use case notifications are designed for.

distractor_notes.B: UI policies change form visibility/behavior. They don't send email.
distractor_notes.C: ACLs control access, not communications.
distractor_notes.D: window.alert is a browser popup for the current user. Notifications need to reach the assignee even when they're not on the form.

stem: What is the role of email properties (the email-related system properties) on an instance?

options.text: They control instance-level email behavior such as sending enable/disable, test mode, SMTP/IMAP configuration values, and reply parsing settings.
They store the personal email signature for every user.
They cache outbound email attachments for performance.
They define the user's preferred font for the inbox UI.

rationale: Email properties are the instance-level switches that control how the platform sends and receives email — enable/disable sending, test mode, mail server configuration, and how inbound replies are interpreted.

distractor_notes.B: Personal signatures are user-level settings, not instance email properties.
distractor_notes.C: Attachment caching isn't what email properties are for.
distractor_notes.D: Inbox UI fonts are unrelated to email properties.

stem: Before exporting an update set from a source instance, what state should it normally be set to?

options.text: In Progress
Complete
Ignored
Build

rationale: Setting an update set to Complete signals that you're done making changes inside it and that it's ready to be picked up by a target instance. In Progress sets aren't intended for promotion.

distractor_notes.A: In Progress means you're still capturing changes. Promote a Complete set, not an in-progress one.
distractor_notes.C: Ignored update sets aren't promoted at all.
distractor_notes.D: There is no 'Build' state in the update set lifecycle.

stem: On the target (test or production) instance, what is the typical order for applying an update set received from another instance?

options.text: Retrieve → Preview → Commit
Commit → Retrieve → Preview
Preview → Commit → Retrieve
Export → Import → Validate

rationale: On the target instance you Retrieve the remote update set (pull it across), Preview it (resolve any collisions or warnings), and then Commit it (apply the changes to the instance). Doing those steps out of order is the classic foot-gun.

distractor_notes.B: Committing before retrieving is impossible — there's nothing to commit yet.
distractor_notes.C: Preview comes after Retrieve, not first.
distractor_notes.D: Export/Import/Validate isn't the supported update-set vocabulary.

stem: During preview, the target instance reports an update set collision. What is the correct response?

options.text: Investigate the collision, choose to accept remote, skip, or merge as appropriate, then commit.
Force-commit without resolving — collisions are informational only.
Delete the target record manually, then re-preview.
Restart the instance to clear the collision cache.

rationale: Collisions surface during preview so the admin can decide what to do per change — accept the incoming change, skip it, or merge — before committing. That deliberation is the whole point of the preview step.

distractor_notes.B: Commits don't ignore unresolved problems quietly. The preview step exists so problems are addressed first.
distractor_notes.C: Deleting target records by hand is dangerous and not the supported workflow for collision resolution.
distractor_notes.D: Restarting doesn't change the underlying conflict; the data is still incompatible.

stem: Which type of change is NOT captured in a standard update set?

options.text: A new business rule script.
A new UI policy.
A new incident record submitted by an end user.
A new client script.

rationale: Update sets capture configuration changes — scripts, policies, forms, fields, and so on. Operational data records (an incident the team logged today) are not configuration and aren't carried in update sets.

distractor_notes.A: Business rules are configuration — they are captured.
distractor_notes.B: UI policies are configuration — they are captured.
distractor_notes.D: Client scripts are configuration — they are captured.

stem: Where does an administrator change the company logo that appears in the Next Experience global header?

options.text: Through the platform's branding/Next Experience configuration that updates the instance logo.
By renaming the favicon.svg in the OS file system.
By writing a script include named CompanyLogo.
By editing the user's profile picture.

rationale: The instance logo for the Next Experience header is changed through the platform's branding configuration — the supported, upgrade-safe path. It updates centrally and applies for all users.

distractor_notes.B: Instances aren't browsed as files; you can't rename favicon assets on a host file system.
distractor_notes.C: Script includes are reusable server scripts. They aren't where you set the logo.
distractor_notes.D: A user's profile picture is just their avatar — not the company branding.

references.title: Change instance banner logo in Next Experience

stem: Which statement is true about a custom scoped application?

options.text: Its resources are namespaced and the application controls how other scopes may read or write them.
It is automatically global — all scopes have full access by default.
It cannot have its own update sets.
It cannot define new roles.

rationale: Scoped apps namespace their resources and use explicit access settings to govern what other scopes can do with them. That isolation is what makes scope a useful packaging boundary.

distractor_notes.B: Scoped apps are not global. Cross-scope access is opt-in.
distractor_notes.C: Scoped apps absolutely have their own update tracking.
distractor_notes.D: Scoped apps can define their own roles.

stem: An admin wants to start a new custom application on their developer instance. Which tool is the supported starting point?

options.text: Studio (the application development workspace).
The CMDB Health dashboard.
A Service Portal page builder widget.
Performance Analytics.

rationale: Studio is the application development environment for creating and managing custom applications, their files, and source control. It's the supported entry point for new custom apps.

distractor_notes.B: The CMDB Health dashboard is for CMDB data quality. It doesn't create applications.
distractor_notes.C: Service Portal page builder builds portal pages, not applications.
distractor_notes.D: Performance Analytics is analytics tooling, not an app dev environment.

stem: A developer makes a change while the global Default update set is selected. Where does that change land?

options.text: In the Default update set, which is intended for unintentional or untracked changes and is not recommended for promotion.
In the most recently committed update set on production.
In a temporary in-memory buffer that disappears on logout.
In all open update sets simultaneously.

rationale: The Default update set is a catch-all for changes made when no purposeful set is active. It captures the change but is not the right vehicle for moving deliberate work between instances — always select a named set before making changes you intend to promote.

distractor_notes.B: Production update sets aren't auto-edited by other instances. There's no remote write.
distractor_notes.C: Changes persist; they aren't held in memory only.
distractor_notes.D: There is exactly one current update set at a time per scope.

stem: A change committed via update set unexpectedly broke a related list on production. What is the most appropriate immediate response?

options.text: Use the Back Out option on the committed update set to reverse the captured changes, then investigate.
Disable the entire instance until next maintenance window.
Delete the affected related list manually so users don't see it.
Re-import the same update set a second time.

rationale: Committed update sets can be backed out, which reverses the changes they applied. It's the right first move when a commit causes a regression — restore the prior state, then root-cause the problem on a sub-prod instance.

distractor_notes.B: Disabling the instance is wildly disproportionate and isn't a normal recovery step.
distractor_notes.C: Manual deletes create more drift and don't address the root cause.
distractor_notes.D: Re-importing the same broken change doesn't help.

stem: Which field on the sys_user record, when set to true, marks a user as a VIP and can affect notification behavior?

options.text: active
vip
priority_user
elevated

rationale: The vip boolean field on the sys_user record marks a user as a VIP. This field can be used in notification conditions and business rules to apply special handling.

distractor_notes.A: The active field controls whether the user account is enabled or disabled, not VIP status.
distractor_notes.C: priority_user is not a standard sys_user field.
distractor_notes.D: elevated is not a standard sys_user field.

stem: What is the effect of setting a user's 'active' field to false on their sys_user record?

options.text: The user's records are deleted from the instance
The user can no longer log into the instance
The user's role assignments are permanently removed
The user is moved to an archived user table

rationale: Setting active to false on a sys_user record disables the account, preventing the user from logging in. Their data and records remain intact.

distractor_notes.A: Records are not deleted when a user is deactivated.
distractor_notes.C: Role assignments are retained when a user is deactivated; they take effect again if the user is reactivated.
distractor_notes.D: There is no archived user table in the standard platform.

stem: What is the table name for user records in ServiceNow?

options.text: sys_user_group
sys_user
sys_person
user_profile

rationale: User records in ServiceNow are stored in the sys_user table. Each row represents one authenticated user account.

distractor_notes.A: sys_user_group stores group records, not individual user records.
distractor_notes.C: sys_person is not a standard ServiceNow table.
distractor_notes.D: user_profile is not the standard table for user accounts.

stem: Which table stores group records in ServiceNow?

options.text: sys_user
sys_group
sys_user_group
sys_team

rationale: Group records in ServiceNow are stored in the sys_user_group table. Groups are used for assignments, notifications, and role grants.

distractor_notes.A: sys_user stores individual user records.
distractor_notes.B: sys_group is not a standard ServiceNow table name.
distractor_notes.D: sys_team is not the standard table for groups.

stem: An admin needs to ensure all members of the 'Network' group inherit the network_admin role. What is the most efficient approach?

options.text: Assign the network_admin role directly to each user in the group
Assign the network_admin role to the Network group so all members inherit it
Create a scheduled job that assigns the role nightly
Use an ACL to restrict access based on group membership

rationale: Assigning a role to a group grants that role to all current and future members of the group. This is the most efficient way to manage role inheritance for a set of users.

distractor_notes.A: Assigning roles individually to each user is inefficient and requires manual updates as membership changes.
distractor_notes.C: A scheduled job is unnecessary when role inheritance via group assignment handles this automatically.
distractor_notes.D: ACLs control access to records, not role assignments.

stem: Which field on a sys_user_group record designates the person responsible for managing the group?

options.text: owner
manager
group_lead
supervisor

rationale: The manager field on a sys_user_group record identifies the person responsible for managing the group.

distractor_notes.A: owner is not the standard field for group management in sys_user_group.
distractor_notes.C: group_lead is not a standard sys_user_group field.
distractor_notes.D: supervisor is not a standard sys_user_group field.

stem: Which role in ServiceNow contains all other roles and grants complete administrative access?

options.text: itil
admin
security_admin
superuser

rationale: The admin role in ServiceNow grants full administrative access to the core platform configuration. It contains all other roles implicitly.

distractor_notes.A: itil grants access to ITSM process modules but is a limited operational role, not a superadmin role.
distractor_notes.C: security_admin is a specialized role for security administration, not a full admin role.
distractor_notes.D: superuser is not a standard ServiceNow role.

stem: A scoped application defines a role called x_acme_app.approver. A user must have this role to approve records in the app. How is this role typically granted?

options.text: It is automatically granted to all admin users
It must be assigned directly to users or groups through the Roles related list
It is inherited from the itil role automatically
It is activated when the plugin for the scoped app is installed

rationale: Application-specific roles defined in a scoped app (like x_acme_app.approver) must be explicitly assigned to users or groups through the Roles related list on the user or group record.

distractor_notes.A: Admin does not automatically inherit application-specific scoped roles unless explicitly configured.
distractor_notes.C: itil is an ITSM role unrelated to custom scoped application roles.
distractor_notes.D: Plugin installation activates features but does not auto-grant scoped roles to users.

stem: What is the effect of a role containing another role in ServiceNow?

options.text: The child role is deprecated when the parent role is assigned
Users with the parent role automatically have the permissions of all contained roles
The contained role must also be assigned separately to take effect
Contained roles only apply in global scope

rationale: When a role contains another role, users assigned the parent role automatically receive all permissions granted by the contained (child) roles. This is how role inheritance works in ServiceNow.

distractor_notes.A: Contained roles are not deprecated; they are inherited.
distractor_notes.C: Contained roles do not need to be separately assigned; the parent role grants them automatically.
distractor_notes.D: Role containment works across scopes, not just global scope.

stem: Before activating a plugin, what should an administrator verify first?

options.text: That the plugin is listed in the ServiceNow Store
That the plugin has not already been activated on the instance
That all existing update sets have been committed
That the instance is running the latest release

rationale: Before requesting or activating a plugin, admins should check whether the plugin has already been activated on the instance to avoid duplicate activation attempts.

distractor_notes.A: Not all plugins are in the Store; some are available through the Application Manager regardless.
distractor_notes.C: Committing update sets is a pre-deployment best practice but is not the first verification step for plugin activation.
distractor_notes.D: Plugin activation is not restricted to the latest release.

stem: Where does an administrator navigate to activate a plugin in ServiceNow?

options.text: System Properties > Plugins
All > System Applications > All Available Applications > All
All > System Definition > Plugins
Admin Center > Plugins

rationale: To activate a plugin, navigate to All > System Applications > All Available Applications > All, then find the plugin using filter criteria or search and select Install.

distractor_notes.A: System Properties is for configuration settings, not plugin activation.
distractor_notes.C: All > System Definition > Plugins is an older navigation path; the current path is through System Applications.
distractor_notes.D: Admin Center is a configuration hub, not where plugins are activated.

stem: When domain separation and delegated admin are enabled, what domain must the activating admin be in to avoid a plugin activation error?

options.text: The top-level domain of the organization
The global domain
The admin's home domain
Any domain with the plugin_admin role

rationale: When domain separation and delegated admin are enabled, the administrative user activating a plugin must be in the global domain. Otherwise, an error appears indicating another operation is running.

distractor_notes.A: The top-level organizational domain is not the same as the global domain in domain separation.
distractor_notes.C: The admin's home domain is insufficient; global domain is required.
distractor_notes.D: plugin_admin is not a documented role for this requirement; being in the global domain is the requirement.

stem: Where can lesser-used system properties that are not on a standard form be found and edited?

options.text: In the System Dictionary
In the System Property [sys_properties] table
In the System Definition > Scripts module
In the Update Set picker

rationale: Some lesser-used system properties exist only in the System Property [sys_properties] table and are not available on the standard system properties forms. Admins can access and add them directly from this table.

distractor_notes.A: The System Dictionary defines table and field schema, not system properties.
distractor_notes.C: Scripts module is for server-side scripts, not property configuration.
distractor_notes.D: The Update Set picker tracks configuration changes, not property values.

stem: What does the system property 'com.glide.attachment.max_size' control?

options.text: The maximum number of attachments per record
The maximum file attachment size in megabytes
The allowed file extension types for attachments
The maximum total storage for all attachments

rationale: The com.glide.attachment.max_size property sets the maximum file attachment size in megabytes. The default value is 1024 (1GB).

distractor_notes.A: There is no standard property limiting the number of attachments per record.
distractor_notes.C: Allowed file extensions are controlled through a separate security property, not com.glide.attachment.max_size.
distractor_notes.D: This property controls per-file size, not total instance storage.

stem: An admin wants to add a custom module to the Application Navigator for easy access to a frequently used system property list. What is the recommended approach?

options.text: Edit the global CSS to add a shortcut link
Add a module in the Application Navigator pointing to the sys_properties table
Create a homepage widget linking to the property list
Use the Admin Center to pin the property

rationale: Administrators can add a module in the application navigator to access the list of system properties. This module provides easy access to add or edit properties in the System Properties table.

distractor_notes.A: CSS modifications are for styling, not application navigator modules.
distractor_notes.C: A homepage widget is a reporting/visualization tool, not the recommended approach for property access.
distractor_notes.D: Admin Center is for application management, not creating custom navigator modules.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a component that an administrator specifies when creating an email notification?

options.text: When to send the notification
Who receives the notification
The physical email server to use
What content is in the notification

rationale: When creating an email notification, administrators specify when to send it, who receives it, what content it contains, and whether it can be delivered as a digest. The physical email server is an instance-level configuration, not part of the individual notification record.

distractor_notes.A: When to send is one of the four key notification components.
distractor_notes.B: Who receives is one of the four key notification components.
distractor_notes.D: Content is one of the four key notification components.

stem: What is an email watermark in ServiceNow notifications?

options.text: A logo image embedded in the email header
A unique label generated at the bottom of each notification email to match incoming email to existing records
A legal disclaimer automatically appended to all outgoing emails
A read-receipt request attached to each notification

rationale: By default, a unique watermark label is generated at the bottom of each notification email. It allows the system to match incoming email replies to the correct existing records.

distractor_notes.A: A watermark is a unique tracking label, not a logo image.
distractor_notes.C: Legal disclaimers are a separate configuration from watermarks.
distractor_notes.D: Watermarks enable record matching, not read receipts.

stem: Can a ServiceNow instance send or receive encrypted email messages?

options.text: Yes, using the Encrypted Email plugin
Yes, if TLS is configured on the mail server
No — the system strips the body of encrypted emails because it cannot process encrypted content
Yes, but only for outgoing emails

rationale: ServiceNow instances cannot send or receive encrypted email messages. The system strips out the body of the encrypted email because it cannot process the encrypted content in plain text or HTML.

distractor_notes.A: There is no Encrypted Email plugin that enables this capability.
distractor_notes.B: TLS encrypts the transport channel but the email body encryption ServiceNow cannot process is end-to-end content encryption.
distractor_notes.D: The limitation applies to both sending and receiving encrypted emails.

stem: What is an email digest in ServiceNow?

options.text: A log of all sent email notifications for a day
A single email that summarizes activity for a notification and its target records during a specified time interval
An archive of all emails older than 30 days
A compressed attachment containing multiple email threads

rationale: An email digest is a single email summarizing activity for a selected notification and its target records during a specified time interval, reducing notification volume when frequent updates occur.

distractor_notes.A: An email digest is not a log; it is a consolidated outgoing summary email.
distractor_notes.C: Email archives are managed through the email retention feature, not digests.
distractor_notes.D: A digest is a consolidated notification email, not a compressed attachment.

stem: What is captured in a standard update set?

options.text: Data records such as incidents and changes
Configuration changes such as form layouts, business rules, and scripts
User account changes and role assignments
All database transactions since the last commit

rationale: Update sets capture configuration changes — such as form layouts, business rules, client scripts, and UI policies — allowing them to be moved between instances. Data records are not captured.

distractor_notes.A: Data records (incidents, changes) are not captured in standard update sets.
distractor_notes.C: User account changes and role assignments are data-level changes not typically captured in update sets.
distractor_notes.D: Update sets capture specific configuration changes, not all database transactions.

stem: What state should an update set be in before it can be exported from a source instance?

options.text: In Progress
Complete
Loaded
Previewed

rationale: An update set must be set to Complete state before it can be exported. This signals that the changes are finalized and ready for migration.

distractor_notes.A: An In Progress update set is still being built; it cannot be exported yet.
distractor_notes.C: Loaded is a state on the target instance after import, not a source export state.
distractor_notes.D: Previewed is a state on the target instance during the review process before committing.

stem: On a target instance, what happens during the Preview step of applying an update set?

options.text: The changes are committed to the instance immediately
The system checks for collisions and potential issues before committing
The update set is exported back to the source instance for review
The system creates a backup of all current configuration

rationale: During preview, the target instance checks for collisions with existing configuration and flags potential issues. The admin reviews these before deciding to commit or skip individual changes.

distractor_notes.A: Preview does not commit changes; it is a pre-commit review step.
distractor_notes.C: Preview is performed on the target, not exported back to source.
distractor_notes.D: ServiceNow does not create a full configuration backup automatically during preview.

stem: A developer accidentally leaves the Default update set selected and makes a configuration change. Where will that change be recorded?

options.text: The change is discarded since the Default set cannot record changes
The change is recorded in the Default update set for the current application scope
The system prompts the developer to select a proper update set before saving
The change is recorded in the last used named update set

rationale: When the Default update set is selected, any configuration changes are recorded into it. The Default set captures changes that were made without explicitly selecting a named update set.

distractor_notes.A: The Default update set does record changes; it is a valid (if undesirable) destination.
distractor_notes.C: The system does not prompt the developer; it silently records to the Default set.
distractor_notes.D: The change goes to whatever update set is currently selected, which in this case is Default.

stem: Which type of change is typically NOT captured in a standard update set?

options.text: Business rules
Client scripts
Data records such as users and incidents
Form layouts

rationale: Standard update sets capture configuration metadata (business rules, scripts, form layouts, etc.) but do not capture data records such as user accounts or incident records.

distractor_notes.A: Business rules are configuration and are captured in update sets.
distractor_notes.B: Client scripts are configuration and are captured in update sets.
distractor_notes.D: Form layouts are configuration and are captured in update sets.

stem: A committed update set broke a related list on production. What should the admin do first?

options.text: Delete the update set records from the production database
Use the Back Out option on the update set to revert the changes
Re-import and re-commit the same update set
Manually restore the previous form layout from memory

rationale: Update sets support a Back Out option that reverts committed changes. This is the proper mechanism to undo a problematic committed update set.

distractor_notes.A: Deleting database records directly is destructive and not the proper approach.
distractor_notes.C: Re-committing the same update set would not fix the issue; it would apply the same broken changes again.
distractor_notes.D: Manual restoration is error-prone and unnecessary when the Back Out feature exists.

stem: What is the primary purpose of application scope in ServiceNow?

options.text: To limit the number of records a user can create per day
To isolate application artifacts and prevent naming conflicts between applications
To define which users have access to a given module
To specify the ServiceNow release a custom application targets

rationale: Application scope in ServiceNow isolates artifacts (tables, scripts, forms) within a namespace, preventing naming conflicts between different applications and protecting application integrity.

distractor_notes.A: Record creation limits are not the purpose of application scope.
distractor_notes.C: Access to modules is controlled by roles and ACLs, not application scope directly.
distractor_notes.D: Application scope defines a namespace, not the target release.

stem: What prefix do custom scoped application artifacts use in their names?

options.text: sys_
custom_
x_<vendor>_<app>_
app_

rationale: Custom scoped application artifacts use the prefix x_<vendor>_<app>_ (e.g., x_acme_procurement_) to namespace them and prevent conflicts with other applications or the base platform.

distractor_notes.A: sys_ is the prefix for core ServiceNow platform tables and artifacts.
distractor_notes.B: custom_ is not a standard ServiceNow prefix.
distractor_notes.D: app_ is not a standard ServiceNow scoped application prefix.

stem: An admin wants to reduce notification volume for users who receive frequent updates to the same record type. Which feature should they enable on the notification?

options.text: Email watermark
Mandatory notification flag
Email digest
Subscription-based notification

rationale: An email digest consolidates multiple notification emails into a single summary email for a specified time interval, reducing notification volume when frequent updates occur.

distractor_notes.A: Watermarks are for matching incoming replies to records, not reducing volume.
distractor_notes.B: Mandatory notifications cannot be unsubscribed from; they increase rather than reduce volume concerns.
distractor_notes.D: Subscription-based notifications let users choose which notifications to receive but do not consolidate them.

stem: What is the default format for new email notifications created in ServiceNow?

options.text: Plain text
Rich HTML
Markdown
XML

rationale: Rich HTML is the default format for all new email notifications. It provides advantages including WYSIWYG editing, reusable mail scripts, and automatic conversion of relative URLs to absolute links.

distractor_notes.A: Plain text is not the default; rich HTML is.
distractor_notes.C: Markdown is not a supported format for ServiceNow email notifications.
distractor_notes.D: XML is not the email format for notifications.

stem: Where in System Properties is the property to control allowed attachment file extensions located?

options.text: System Properties > General
System Properties > Security
System Properties > Email
System Properties > Attachments

rationale: Attachment-related security properties, including the maximum file size and MIME type checking, are found under System Properties > Security.

distractor_notes.A: System Properties > General controls general instance settings, not attachment security.
distractor_notes.C: System Properties > Email controls email server configuration, not attachments.
distractor_notes.D: There is no standard System Properties > Attachments category; security-related attachment settings are under Security.

stem: Which feature allows users to control which non-mandatory notifications they receive?

options.text: Email digests
Subscription-based notifications
Watermarks
Email templates

rationale: Subscription-based notifications allow users to subscribe to or unsubscribe from notifications that are not mandatory, giving users control over which alerts they receive.

distractor_notes.A: Email digests consolidate frequency, not which notifications are received.
distractor_notes.C: Watermarks match incoming emails to records; they do not control subscription preferences.
distractor_notes.D: Email templates define content structure; they do not control subscription.

stem: A developer exports an update set from development and imports it to a UAT instance. After preview, there are no collisions. What is the next step?

options.text: Export the update set from UAT to production directly
Commit the update set on UAT to apply the changes
Set the update set state back to In Progress on UAT
Run validate-questions on UAT to confirm correctness

rationale: After preview with no collisions, the next step is to commit the update set on the target instance, which applies all captured configuration changes.

distractor_notes.A: The update set must be committed to UAT first; you would then go through the same import/preview/commit process for production.
distractor_notes.C: Setting the state back to In Progress is for source instances where more changes need to be added, not for target instances after a clean preview.
distractor_notes.D: validate-questions is a GlideUp project tool, not a ServiceNow platform step.

stem: What is the primary purpose of user impersonation in ServiceNow?

options.text: To permanently assume another user's identity for administrative tasks
To temporarily simulate another user's session to test their experience
To elevate the impersonated user's roles for a single transaction
To create a copy of the user's account for troubleshooting

rationale: User impersonation allows an admin to temporarily simulate another user's session — seeing exactly what that user sees — which is useful for testing configurations, troubleshooting access issues, and verifying role-based behavior.

distractor_notes.A: Impersonation is temporary and session-scoped, not permanent.
distractor_notes.C: Impersonation does not elevate the target user's roles; it simulates their existing access.
distractor_notes.D: No copy of the user account is created during impersonation.

stem: Which role is required to impersonate another user in ServiceNow?

options.text: itil
admin
security_admin
impersonator

rationale: The admin role is required to impersonate another user. The keyboard shortcut Control+Shift+i (Windows) / Command+Shift+i (macOS) opens the impersonation dialog.

distractor_notes.A: itil is an ITSM operational role and does not grant impersonation capability.
distractor_notes.C: security_admin is for security features, not user impersonation.
distractor_notes.D: impersonator is not a standard ServiceNow role.

stem: An admin wants a specific notification to always be delivered to recipients, even if they have unsubscribed from that notification type. Which feature should they use?

options.text: Email digest
Mandatory notification
Email template
Watermark

rationale: Mandatory notifications cannot be unsubscribed from by users. Admins can make specific notifications mandatory to ensure critical communications are always delivered.

distractor_notes.A: Email digests consolidate frequency but do not override user subscription settings.
distractor_notes.C: Email templates define notification content structure; they do not control mandatory delivery.
distractor_notes.D: Watermarks are for record matching on inbound emails, not controlling delivery.

stem: A system property does not exist in a base instance. What must an admin do to use it?

options.text: Upgrade to the next ServiceNow release
Request ServiceNow support to enable it
Add the property to the System Property [sys_properties] table manually
Install a plugin to activate the property

rationale: Some system properties do not exist in a base instance but can be added by creating a new record in the System Property [sys_properties] table and setting the desired value.

distractor_notes.A: Upgrading releases does not add custom system properties.
distractor_notes.B: Standard system properties can be added without contacting support.
distractor_notes.D: Installing a plugin is unrelated to adding a custom system property.

stem: Which table stores the many-to-many relationship between users and groups in ServiceNow?

options.text: sys_user_group
sys_user_grmember
sys_user_has_group
sys_group_member

rationale: The sys_user_grmember table stores the many-to-many relationships between users and groups, recording which users are members of which groups.

distractor_notes.A: sys_user_group stores the group definitions themselves, not the membership relationships.
distractor_notes.C: sys_user_has_group is not a standard ServiceNow table.
distractor_notes.D: sys_group_member is not a standard ServiceNow table.

stem: What state does an update set enter on the target instance when it has been imported but not yet previewed?

options.text: Complete
In Progress
Loaded
Committed

rationale: After an update set is imported to the target instance, it enters the Loaded state. The admin then runs Preview before committing.

distractor_notes.A: Complete is the state set on the source instance before export.
distractor_notes.B: In Progress means the update set is being actively modified on the source instance.
distractor_notes.D: Committed is the state after the update set has been successfully applied to the target.

stem: An admin converts an existing notification to rich HTML format. Which is an advantage the docs describe for rich HTML notifications?

options.text: They are delivered faster than plain text emails
Relative URLs in the notification body are automatically converted to absolute links
They bypass spam filters on recipient mail servers
They support end-to-end encryption

rationale: Rich HTML notifications automatically convert relative URLs (such as incident links) to absolute links, preventing broken links in the email content.

distractor_notes.A: Rich HTML does not affect email delivery speed.
distractor_notes.C: Rich HTML does not bypass spam filters; deliverability depends on server configuration.
distractor_notes.D: ServiceNow cannot send or receive encrypted emails.

stem: A developer in a custom scoped app tries to modify a base platform business rule. What protection does application scope provide in this scenario?

options.text: The developer is automatically granted admin role to make the change
The scoped app cannot modify base platform artifacts that are outside its scope without explicit cross-scope access grants
The change is allowed but is logged for security review
The change is applied only in the developer's test instance, not globally

rationale: Application scope protects platform integrity by restricting scoped applications from modifying artifacts outside their scope. Cross-scope access must be explicitly granted.

distractor_notes.A: Scope does not auto-grant admin access.
distractor_notes.C: The change is blocked, not just logged.
distractor_notes.D: Scope restrictions apply regardless of the instance type.

stem: When a notification email is sent as an SMS, what part of the email does the system use as the SMS message by default?

options.text: The email body
The email subject line
The first paragraph of the email body
A separately stored SMS template

rationale: When a notification is delivered via SMS, the system uses the subject line of the email notification and converts it to the SMS message by default. Admins can define an alternate SMS message if needed.

distractor_notes.A: The email body is not used by default for SMS; the subject line is.
distractor_notes.C: Only the first paragraph is not the default; it is the subject line.
distractor_notes.D: A separate SMS template can be defined but is not the default behavior.

stem: When activating a plugin and the admin cannot find it in the plugin list, what should they do?

options.text: Check if the plugin is already active using the Application Manager
Request the plugin from ServiceNow personnel
Install it from the ServiceNow developer portal
Increase the filter limit in the All Available Applications module

rationale: If a plugin cannot be found in the available plugins list, the admin may need to request it from ServiceNow personnel, as some plugins require special licensing or activation.

distractor_notes.A: Checking if it is already active is the first pre-activation step, but if it is not found at all in the list, requesting from ServiceNow is appropriate.
distractor_notes.C: There is no general developer portal for downloading plugins to install manually.
distractor_notes.D: Increasing a filter limit is not the solution for a missing plugin.

stem: A service desk manager leaves the company. Their sys_user record is deactivated. What happens to incidents currently assigned to that user's group?

options.text: All incidents are immediately reassigned to the group manager
The incidents remain assigned to the group; the group's other members can still work them
All incidents are set to Unassigned automatically
The group is also deactivated since the manager is gone

rationale: Deactivating a user's sys_user record only disables their login. Group membership and record assignments are not automatically changed. Incidents assigned to the group remain assigned to the group for other members to work.

distractor_notes.A: No automatic reassignment to the group manager occurs when a user is deactivated.
distractor_notes.C: Incidents are not automatically unassigned when a group member or manager is deactivated.
distractor_notes.D: The group record is independent of any individual user's active status.

stem: An admin sets com.glide.attachment.max_size to an empty value. What is the result?

options.text: All file uploads are blocked until a value is entered
Attachments are allowed up to a maximum of 1KB
The default of 1024MB applies automatically
Attachments of unlimited size are allowed

rationale: An empty value in the com.glide.attachment.max_size field allows attachments up to a maximum of 1KB. This is a known edge case — the default 1024MB applies when the property holds the value '1024', not when it is blank.

distractor_notes.A: File uploads are not blocked by an empty property; they are limited to 1KB.
distractor_notes.C: The 1024MB default applies when the property value is set to 1024, not when it is empty.
distractor_notes.D: An empty value does not unlock unlimited upload size; it restricts to 1KB.

stem: What is the recommended order for applying multiple related update sets on a target instance?

options.text: Alphabetical order by update set name
Apply them in the order they were created on the source instance
Commit the largest update set first
Apply them in any order since ServiceNow resolves dependencies automatically

rationale: Related update sets should be applied in the same order they were created on the source instance to respect dependencies between configuration changes.

distractor_notes.A: Alphabetical order does not respect creation sequence or dependencies.
distractor_notes.C: Size of the update set is not the correct ordering criterion.
distractor_notes.D: ServiceNow does not automatically resolve dependency order between related update sets.

stem: Which two methods can an administrator use to grant a role to a user in ServiceNow?

options.text: Assign the role directly on the user's sys_user record via the Roles related list
Assign the user to a group that has the role
Set the user's department to a department that has the role
Enable the role via a system property

rationale: Roles can be granted to users either directly via the Roles related list on the user record, or indirectly by assigning the user to a group that has been granted the role.

distractor_notes.C: Departments do not directly grant roles to users.
distractor_notes.D: System properties do not grant roles to users; roles are assigned through user or group records.

stem: An admin needs the incident assignee to receive an email when an incident is set to Priority 1. Where is this condition defined in the notification record?

options.text: In the Email Template field
In the When to send section of the notification
In the System Property for email triggers
In the Business Rule condition field

rationale: The 'When to send' section of a notification record defines the conditions that trigger the notification, such as when Priority = 1. The 'Who receives' section specifies the assignee as a recipient.

distractor_notes.A: The Email Template defines the content structure, not the trigger conditions.
distractor_notes.C: System properties configure the email server behavior, not individual notification triggers.
distractor_notes.D: Business rules are separate automation records; notification conditions are defined on the notification itself.

stem: What is an update set collision?

options.text: When two update sets are exported at the same time from different instances
When a change in the update set conflicts with an existing customization on the target instance
When an update set exceeds the maximum allowed file size for import
When a plugin is activated while an update set is in progress

rationale: A collision occurs during preview when the update set tries to apply a change that conflicts with a customization already present on the target instance. The admin must resolve these before committing.

distractor_notes.A: Simultaneous exports from different instances do not constitute a collision.
distractor_notes.C: There is no standard maximum file size for update set import that creates a 'collision'.
distractor_notes.D: Plugin activation during an update set does not create an update set collision.

stem: What is the global application scope used for in ServiceNow?

options.text: It is a restricted scope used only by ServiceNow for platform tables
It is the default scope for configurations that apply across all applications and are not isolated to a specific app
It is the scope for the ServiceNow Store applications
It is a read-only scope for viewing platform configurations

rationale: The global scope is the default application scope where configurations that apply across the platform (not isolated to a specific application) are stored. Many core platform configurations exist in global scope.

distractor_notes.A: Global scope is accessible to admins, not restricted to ServiceNow only.
distractor_notes.C: Store applications use their own scoped namespaces, not global scope.
distractor_notes.D: Global scope is not read-only; it is the primary scope for cross-application configurations.

stem: Which type of role assignment takes effect for a user as soon as they are added to a group that has the role?

options.text: Explicit role assignment only
Inherited role from group membership
Delegated role assignment
Temporary role escalation

rationale: When a role is assigned to a group, all users who are members of that group immediately inherit the role. This is role inheritance via group membership.

distractor_notes.A: Explicit role assignment is when the role is directly added to the user record, not via a group.
distractor_notes.C: Delegated roles are a different mechanism for temporary role grants, not the immediate group inheritance described.
distractor_notes.D: Temporary role escalation is not a standard group membership mechanism.

stem: What typically happens when a plugin is installed on a ServiceNow instance?

options.text: The plugin downloads a zip file that the admin must manually extract
An application with components such as tables, roles, and scheduled jobs is installed
The platform is temporarily taken offline during installation
The plugin is applied only to the sandbox environment until promoted

rationale: Activating a plugin installs an application on the instance. Each application consists of components such as tables, user roles, scheduled jobs, and more.

distractor_notes.A: Plugin activation is server-side; there is no zip download or manual extraction for the admin.
distractor_notes.C: Instances do not go offline during plugin activation in standard scenarios.
distractor_notes.D: Plugins are activated directly on the instance; there is no sandbox promotion step.

stem: Which system property location controls MIME type validation for file attachments?

options.text: System Properties > General
System Properties > Email
System Properties > Security
System Properties > CMDB

rationale: MIME type validation for file attachments is controlled through System Properties > Security. The default setting for MIME type validation on a new instance is No (disabled).

distractor_notes.A: General properties control broad platform settings, not MIME validation.
distractor_notes.B: Email properties control mail server behavior, not file attachment MIME checking.
distractor_notes.D: CMDB properties relate to configuration management, not file attachments.

stem: An admin wants to start capturing a specific set of form layout changes for a new incident workspace redesign. What should they do before making any changes?

options.text: Enable tracking mode in System Diagnostics
Create a new named update set and set it as the current update set
Export the current default update set before beginning
Create a backup of the production database

rationale: Before making configuration changes intended for a specific update set, the admin should create a new named update set and set it as the current update set so all subsequent changes are captured in it.

distractor_notes.A: System Diagnostics does not include an update set tracking mode.
distractor_notes.C: Exporting the current default update set does not create a new capture container for the new changes.
distractor_notes.D: Creating a database backup is good practice but is unrelated to update set management.

stem: What does an email template provide in ServiceNow notifications?

options.text: The trigger conditions for when a notification fires
Reusable content for the subject line and message body of notifications
The list of recipients for a notification
The delivery channel selection (email vs SMS)

rationale: Email templates provide reusable content for the subject line and message body of email notifications. They can be referenced across multiple notifications to maintain consistent messaging.

distractor_notes.A: Trigger conditions are defined in the 'When to send' section of the notification, not the template.
distractor_notes.C: Recipients are defined in the 'Who receives' section of the notification.
distractor_notes.D: Delivery channel (email vs SMS) is a notification-level setting, not part of the email template.

stem: During preview of an update set on the target instance, a collision is detected for a business rule that was customized locally. What options does the admin have?

options.text: The update set must be rejected entirely; partial commits are not allowed
The admin can accept the incoming version, skip the colliding record, or manually merge the changes
The collision is automatically resolved using the most recent timestamp
The local version is always preserved and the incoming change is discarded

rationale: When a collision is detected during preview, the admin can choose to accept the incoming version from the update set, skip that individual record, or manually resolve by merging both sets of changes.

distractor_notes.A: Partial commits are possible; individual colliding records can be skipped.
distractor_notes.C: Collisions are not automatically resolved by timestamp; they require manual admin decision.
distractor_notes.D: The local version is not automatically preserved; the admin makes the decision.
